beats.text: Before modern AI, every model crawled through sentences like reading text through a straw—strictly one word at a time.
beats.visual_focus: A narrow slit moving tediously across a long line of sequence tokens, freezing GPU threads

beats.text: Sequential recurrence forced parallel supercomputers to wait like cars stuck at a single-lane toll booth, crippling training throughput across clusters.
beats.visual_focus: Massive multi-core compute engines idling while waiting for a single sequential step to resolve

beats.text: The Transformer discarded recurrence entirely, deploying multi-head attention to forge direct, simultaneous connections between all sequence tokens in parallel.
beats.visual_focus: A sudden geometric explosion where every word projects all-to-all connection lines at once

beats.text: Training dropped to three point five days on eight GPUs, setting an unprecedented state-of-the-art forty-one point eight BLEU translation score.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: Dude, this is actually solid. The toll booth analogy for GPUs waiting on recurrent sequential passes makes total sense without feeling like baby talk. You didn't waste time with 'Welcome back guys' or 'In this video,' you just jumped straight into why RNNs sucked on hardware. Beat 4 drops Q, K, V and dot-product fast, but in the context of sequence-wide parallel math, it totally clicks.
